sections.title: Innovation and Entrepreneurship
sections.description: This quarter-length course serves as the second half of the PhD sequence in entrepreneurship and innovation (MGMT 9370 & MGMT 9470). Our six sessions examine innovation as a process of search and knowledge production: beginning with how innovators navigate technological landscapes, moving through the role of science as a map for innovation and the technologies that reshape knowledge production, and concluding with the organizational and market forces that shape which ideas are pursued and developed. Alongside the two to three primary assigned readings per session, we encourage you to select one additional reading from the optional list to tailor the course to your own research interests. In each session, you will brief the class on your selected reading to broaden our collective scope and fuel a richer, more comprehensive dialogue.
